mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 2% signals an easing monetary policy that compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% indicates labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 5.5%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production below 110 and housing starts below 1000 signal a broad economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 110 and HOUST < 1000, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY) triggers monetary tightening expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL > 2.5% YoY periods, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS above 0.5% MoM) supports consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth > 0.5% MoM, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales below 380 billion dollars indicate weak consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS < 380000, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in industrial production below 110 and unemployment rate above 5.5% signal a dual contraction in production and labor markets, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 110 and UNRATE > 5.5, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (above 2% annualized) during economic expansion phases supports corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In GDPC1 growth > 2% annualized periods, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.
